title: Laser ablation nudging and its dual-use problem
bottleneck: Ground- or space-based lasers could nudge small debris by vaporizing surface material to create ablation thrust — elegant for the small-debris population that cannot be grappled. But a laser powerful enough to perturb debris is powerful enough to damage active satellites, making every debris laser a latent space weapon. Verification, targeting transparency, and international trust frameworks do not exist, and atmospheric distortion limits ground-based effectiveness. The technology is hostage to its military implications.
why_it_blocks: Small debris cannot be grappled, so non-contact methods are the only removal path — yet the best non-contact method is politically undeployable.
current_state: Lab and simulation studies only; some proposals for space-based laser demonstrators exist. No operational debris laser and no governance framework.
